status: Phase B. Module 5 claim-vs-evidence sort. Evidence cards cite research/sources.md rows; claim cards are statements people make, written for the activity (constructed for teaching purposes).

categories.label: Evidence (an observation or measurement, with a source)
Claim (a conclusion someone draws, which needs evidence)

cards.text: USGS photos from the same viewpoint: ice fills the valley in 1941; it is gone from view in 2004.
cards.why: A dated observation with a named source.

cards.text: USGS caption: from 1941 to 1950 Muir Glacier retreated more than 3 km and thinned more than 100 m.
cards.why: A published measurement, stated as a minimum.

cards.text: NPS: the Little Ice Age advance here reached its maximum about 1750, when general melting began.
cards.why: A dated finding from the park service. It shows the retreat started long before 1941.

cards.text: NPS: seawater undermines tidewater ice fronts, and blocks up to 200 feet high can calve off.
cards.why: A described process at tidewater fronts: one mechanism of ice loss besides melting.

cards.text: NPS: 'The advance or retreat of a glacier reflects many factors: snowfall rate, topography, and climate trends. Tidewater glaciers are even more complicated.'
cards.why: An expert summary of the factors. Treat it as evidence that more than one cause is possible.

cards.text: NPS: heavy snowfall in the Fairweather Mountains means Glacier Bay still has a few stable glaciers.
cards.why: Shows that local snowfall matters: not every glacier in the same region behaves the same way.

cards.text: USGS: White Thunder Ridge was bare in 1941 and 1950 and densely vegetated by 2004.
cards.why: A dated observation of land cover.

cards.text: Muir Glacier retreated only because of recent warming.
cards.why: A conclusion. The evidence (retreat since about 1750, calving) suggests more than one factor, so this claim is too strong.

cards.text: Climate has nothing to do with Muir Glacier's retreat.
cards.why: A conclusion. NPS lists climate trends among the factors, so this claim is too strong the other way.

cards.text: Several factors, including climate and tidewater calving, likely combined to cause the retreat.
cards.why: A conclusion, and the one best supported by these cards. It still needs data such as climate records to weigh each factor.

cards.text: In a few hundred years the ridge will be old-growth forest.
cards.why: A prediction. The NPS succession sequence supports the direction, but no source used here gives the timing at Muir Inlet.
